questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct with reference to the modern periodic table?

options.text: ​Lanthanoids and actinoids are placed in separate panels at the bottom.
Groups are the vertical columns, and periods are horizontal rows.
The second and third periods each contain 8 elements.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The first period contains 8 elements.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **modern periodic table** arranges elements based on their **atomic numbers** in horizontal rows called **periods** and vertical columns called **groups.**
 
• The **first period** of the modern periodic table contains only **two elements: Hydrogen and Helium.**
 
• This is because the first energy level (shell) can hold a maximum of **two electrons.**
 
• Thus, the statement that the first period contains **8 elements** is incorrect.
 
• Subsequent periods contain more elements due to the increasing capacity of energy levels to hold electrons.
 
• For example, the **second period** contains **8 elements**, corresponding to the filling of the 2s and 2p orbitals.
 
• The periodic table is divided into blocks based on the **sub-shells** being filled (s, p, d, f blocks).
 
• The placement of elements reflects their **properties** and provides a systematic way to study chemical behavior.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lanthanoids and actinoids are placed in separate panels at the bottom**__

 __
 
• **Lanthanoids** and **actinoids** are the f-block elements of the periodic table.
 
• They are placed separately to maintain the **structure and readability** of the table.
 
• **Lanthanoids** are elements with atomic numbers 57 to 71, while **actinoids** are elements with atomic numbers 89 to 103.
 
• These elements exhibit **unique electronic configurations** and properties, such as their use in **magnets, lasers, and nuclear reactors.**
 
 
 
• **Groups are the vertical columns, and periods are horizontal rows**__
 __
 
• The modern periodic table has **18 groups** and **7 periods.**
 
• **Groups** are vertical columns where elements have similar **valence electron configurations** and chemical properties.
 
• **Periods** are horizontal rows representing elements with increasing atomic numbers.
 
• For example, elements in Group 1 are the **alkali metals,** while those in Group 17 are the **halogens.**
 
 
 
• **The second and third periods each contain 8 elements**__
 
 
• The **second period** contains elements from **Lithium to Neon**, corresponding to the filling of 2s and 2p orbitals.
 
• The **third period** contains elements from **Sodium to Argon**, corresponding to the filling of 3s and 3p orbitals.
 
• This pattern reflects the **quantum mechanical arrangement of electrons** in atoms.

• It supports a variety of platforms, including **laptops, desktops, Raspberry Pi, and mobile devices.**
 
• Kali Linux allows ethical hackers and security professionals to efficiently perform **vulnerability assessments, security audits, and penetration testing.**
 
• The operating system is open-source and provides strong community support, making it an excellent choice for **cybersecurity enthusiasts and professionals.**
 
• Kali Linux also includes advanced features such as **customizable penetration testing environments, live boot options, and multi-language support.**

• **Ubuntu LTS (Long Term Support)** versions receive regular updates and security patches for up to five years, making it ideal for stable and reliable systems.
 
• While it is versatile, it lacks the specialized tools pre-installed in **Kali Linux** that are essential for penetration testing and ethical hacking.

questions.question: Which of the following input devices primarily translates physical, real-world movements into digital signals that can be interpreted by a computer system for tasks such as navigation and object manipulation in a graphical environment?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mouse**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **mouse** is a crucial input device that translates **physical movement**, such as dragging or clicking, into **digital signals** for a computer system.
 
• It is widely used for tasks like **navigation**, **object selection**, and **manipulation** in graphical environments (e.g., operating systems, video games).
 
• The movement of the mouse is detected by either **mechanical components** (in older models) or advanced **optical sensors** (in modern devices).
 
• These movements are then converted into corresponding **cursor movements** on the computer screen, allowing precise control.
 
• The mouse often comes with additional buttons and a scroll wheel, enabling users to execute commands such as **clicking**, **dragging**, **scrolling**, and **double-clicking**.
 
• It can be connected to a computer via a **USB cable** or wirelessly through **Bluetooth**.
 
• The mouse has become an essential tool for **interactive user interfaces** and is pivotal in various fields such as **designing, gaming, and data management**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scanner**__

 __
 
• A **scanner** is an input device used to convert **physical documents or images** into **digital format**.
 
• It is not used for real-time navigation or object manipulation, but rather for **digitizing printed material**.
 
• Examples of scanners include **flatbed scanners** and **barcode scanners**.
 
 
 
• **Microphone**__
 __
 
• A **microphone** captures **audio signals** (sound) and converts them into **digital signals** for processing by a computer.
 
• It is used primarily for applications such as **voice recording**, **speech recognition**, and **communication**.
 
• However, it does not assist in navigation or graphical tasks.
 
 
 
• **Keyboard**__
 
 
• A **keyboard** is an input device that allows users to input **text, commands, and shortcuts** into a computer system.
 
• It is primarily used for **typing** and interacting with software but does not convert physical movement into digital signals for graphical tasks.
 
• Modern keyboards often come with additional **function keys** and **media controls**.

questions.question: The McMahon Line separates India from which country?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **McMahon Line** is the boundary line that separates **India** from **China**.
 
• It was drawn during the **Simla Convention** of **1914**, between British India and Tibet, with the presence of China.
 
• The line is named after **Sir Henry McMahon**, the then Foreign Secretary of British India, who represented India in the negotiations.
 
• This line is situated in the northeastern region of India, specifically along the state of **Arunachal Pradesh**, which China often claims as part of its territory.
 
• The McMahon Line runs for approximately **550 miles** (885 kilometers).
 
• While India recognizes the McMahon Line as its legal boundary, **China disputes** this line, leading to border tensions between the two nations.
 
• The region around the McMahon Line is geopolitically sensitive and has been the site of conflicts, including the **Sino-Indian War of 1962**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pakistan**__

 __
 
• India shares its western border with **Pakistan**, marked primarily by the **Radcliffe Line**.
 
• The **Radcliffe Line** was drawn during the **partition of India** in **1947**.
 
• The border between India and Pakistan is highly sensitive, with disputes over regions such as **Kashmir**.
 
 
 
• **Nepal**__
 __
 
• India shares an open border with **Nepal**, which is marked by the **Mahakali River** in certain regions.
 
• The **India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship (1950)** governs the bilateral relationship between the two countries.
 
• Citizens of both countries can travel across the border without requiring a visa or passport.
 
 
 
• **Bhutan**__
 
 
• India shares its northeastern border with **Bhutan**.
 
• The border is defined by geographical features such as the **Himalayas**.
 
• India and Bhutan maintain strong diplomatic ties, and India assists Bhutan in its development projects.

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution through the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
• These duties aim to remind citizens of their responsibility to contribute to the **nation's well-being** and ensure a harmonious social environment.
 
• The provision under Article 51A (i) is crucial for promoting a sense of responsibility among citizens to protect public assets and ensure that violence is avoided in public life.
 
• Public property refers to assets owned collectively by society, such as **parks, government buildings, public transport, and infrastructure**.
 
• Abjuring violence is essential for maintaining **peace and order** in society, ensuring that differences are resolved through non-violent means.

• **Article 51A (j)**__

questions.question: Which body took suo motu cognisance of the news titled 'Experts are alarmed as 350 turtles was ashore dead till January 15', published on 16 January 2025?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**National Green Tribunal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** is a specialized judicial body established under the **National Green Tribunal Act, 2010**.
 
• Its primary purpose is to handle cases related to **environmental protection** and the conservation of forests and other natural resources.
 
• The NGT has the authority to take **suo motu cognisance** of environmental issues, which means it can initiate action on its own based on media reports or other information, as in the case of the news about **350 turtles found dead on the shore**.
 
• Such cases are critical for addressing violations of environmental laws and ensuring compliance with the principles of **sustainable development** and **environmental justice**.
 
• The tribunal is empowered to provide relief, compensation, and restitution of property and the environment in such cases.
 
• The NGT operates in a **time-bound manner** to ensure swift disposal of cases and is guided by principles of **natural justice**.
 
• This tribunal has jurisdiction over all civil cases where a substantial question relating to the environment is involved, including those arising under laws like the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**, **Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980**, and **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Supreme Court of India**__

 __
 
• The **Supreme Court** is the highest judicial authority in India, established under **Article 124** of the Constitution.
 
• It primarily deals with constitutional matters, appeals from lower courts, and cases of national importance.
 
• While the Supreme Court can address environmental issues, it does not typically take suo motu cognisance of specific environmental cases like the NGT does.
 
 
 
• **High Court of Tamil Nadu**__
 __
 
• The **High Court of Tamil Nadu** is the principal civil court of original jurisdiction in Tamil Nadu and handles cases under its territorial jurisdiction.
 
• Though High Courts can hear environmental cases, they generally do not have the specialized expertise or mandate of the NGT for addressing environmental violations.
 
 
 
• **High Court of Odisha**__
 
 
• The **High Court of Odisha** is the highest judicial body in the state of Odisha.
 
• It can hear cases concerning environmental issues within its state jurisdiction but lacks the pan-India jurisdiction and specialized focus of the NGT.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states about the establishment of Election Commission in India?

__
 
• **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the **Election Commission of India (ECI)**.
 
• The Election Commission is responsible for the **superintendence, direction, and control** of elections to the Parliament, State Legislatures, and offices of the President and Vice-President of India.
 
• This article vests the power of conducting free and fair elections in an **independent constitutional body**, ensuring the democratic framework of the country.
 
• The Election Commission is a **permanent and independent body** to ensure that elections are conducted in a fair and unbiased manner.
 
• The Commission consists of the **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)** and other Election Commissioners as the President may appoint.
 
• The powers and functions under Article 324 ensure **autonomy and authority** to the Election Commission to maintain the integrity of the electoral process in India.
 
• It is a vital provision to safeguard the principle of **free and fair elections**, which is the cornerstone of a democratic system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 326**__

 __

questions.question: With reference to computer systems, what does CPU stand for?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Central Processing Unit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** is often referred to as the **"brain of the computer"**.
 
• It is responsible for performing **arithmetic, logic, control, and input/output operations** as specified by the instructions in a program.
 
• The CPU comprises three key components:
 
 
• **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU):** Performs arithmetic and logical operations.
 
• **Control Unit (CU):** Directs the operations of the processor and coordinates with other computer components.
 
• **Registers:** Small storage units within the CPU used for quick data access.
 
 
 
• It processes data received from **input devices** and sends the output to **output devices**.
 
• The CPU interacts with the **memory unit** (RAM) to fetch, decode, and execute instructions.
 
• Modern CPUs are designed with **multiple cores**, allowing them to process multiple tasks simultaneously, improving performance.
 
• Examples of CPUs include processors from companies like **Intel (e.g., Core i5, i7)** and **AMD (e.g., Ryzen 5, Ryzen 7)**.
 
• The performance of a CPU is measured in terms of its **clock speed** (e.g., GHz) and the number of **cores**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Computer Processing Utility**__

 __
 
• This term is incorrect as there is no such established term in computer science.
 
• The word "Utility" generally refers to software tools used for system maintenance or performance enhancement, not a hardware component like the CPU.
 
 
 
• **Central Programming Unit**__
 __
 
• This is an incorrect term. The CPU does not specifically deal with programming but rather the execution of instructions from programs.
 
• Programming is typically done using software tools like compilers, interpreters, or IDEs, not the CPU directly.
 
 
 
• **Control Processing Unit**__
 
 
• This term is incorrect. While the CPU includes a **Control Unit (CU)**, the entire unit is not referred to as the "Control Processing Unit."
 
• The Control Unit is just one of the components of the CPU, alongside the **ALU** and **Registers**.

questions.question: What makes DNA the most abundant genetic material?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Its stable double-helical structure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **double-helical structure** of DNA is stabilized by hydrogen bonds between the nitrogenous bases and hydrophobic interactions among the base pairs.
 
• This stable structure ensures the **faithful replication** and preservation of genetic information across generations.
 
• The stability of DNA allows it to resist degradation and maintain its integrity, making it the most **abundant genetic material**.
 
• The backbone of DNA is made up of **phosphate and deoxyribose sugar**, which contributes to its chemical resilience.
 
• The structure also facilitates the precise pairing of bases (adenine with thymine, and cytosine with guanine), ensuring **accurate genetic coding**.
 
• The stability of DNA is further enhanced by its ability to interact with **histones and other proteins**, which help compact and protect it within chromosomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Its high mutation rate**__

 __
 
• A high mutation rate would make DNA unstable and less reliable for preserving genetic information.
 
• While mutations play a role in evolution, excessive mutations can lead to **genetic disorders** and errors in replication.
 
 
 
• **Its interaction with proteins**__
 __
 
• DNA interacts with proteins like histones to form chromatin; however, this feature is not directly responsible for DNA being the most abundant genetic material.
 
• Protein interactions primarily help in **packaging and regulation** of genetic material.
 
 
 
• **Its enzymatic roles**__
 
 
• DNA itself does not perform enzymatic roles; instead, enzymes like DNA polymerase and helicase act on DNA during replication and repair.
 
• Enzymatic roles are more relevant to **RNA**, which can act as a ribozyme (catalytic RNA).

• Each minister is designated as the **political head of his/her ministry**, meaning they are responsible for setting policies, making decisions, and ensuring the implementation of laws within their respective departments.
 
• Ministers work in collaboration with **civil servants** who are tasked with operational execution, providing expertise, and implementing policies laid down by the government.
 
• The political leadership of ministers ensures that the actions of their ministry align with the government’s vision and objectives, as well as the interests of the public.
 
• This structure is derived from the **Westminster system**, where the ministers are accountable to the legislature and indirectly to the public.
 
• The Union Council of Ministers operates under the framework of the **Indian Constitution**, particularly Articles **74** and **75**, which define its composition, functions, and roles.

• **Centralisation of power in local bodies**__
 __
 
• This is incorrect because the Union Council of Ministers is responsible for **national-level governance**, not local bodies. Local governance is handled by **Panchayati Raj Institutions** and urban municipal bodies under the provisions of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **The abolition of the role of the Secretary**__

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction is correct?

options.text: It extends to both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The Supreme Court’s **writ jurisdiction** is provided under **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights**.
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined under **Part III** of the Indian Constitution, including rights such as **Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Constitutional Remedies**, etc.
 
• The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is considered a crucial mechanism for ensuring the protection of citizens' rights and maintaining the rule of law.
 
• The types of writs that can be issued include **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto**.
 
• Article 32 is often referred to as the **"Heart and Soul of the Constitution"**, as described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, due to its significant role in safeguarding Fundamental Rights.
 
• Unlike the High Courts, the Supreme Court’s writ jurisdiction is limited to matters involving Fundamental Rights and does not extend to other legal rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: It extends to both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.**__

 __
 
• This is incorrect because the Supreme Court’s writ jurisdiction under **Article 32** is restricted to the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** only. It does not extend to other legal rights.
 
• However, High Courts under **Article 226** can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: It is exclusive and cannot be exercised by the High Courts.**__
 __
 
• This is incorrect as **High Courts**, under **Article 226**, also have writ jurisdiction, which is broader than the Supreme Court’s jurisdiction under Article 32.
 
• The High Courts can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: It allows the Court to issue writs only against the Central Government.**__
 
 
• This is incorrect as writs can be issued against both the **Central Government**, **State Governments**, and even private individuals or entities where applicable.
